title: Solving versus Verifying: Catching Contradictions in Tax Reasoning Systems
abstract: arXiv:2609.05928v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models now compute correct tax liabilities on over 90% of well-formed cases in statutory benchmarks, which makes them candidates for the tax-advisory and compliance systems that consume such an answer directly. Real legal inputs, however, are frequently defective: required facts are missing, or stated facts contradict one another. Accuracy on clean benchmarks says nothing about how a model behaves then, and a system that computes straight through a defective input returns a confident number with no sign that anything is wrong. This raises two questions: does a model asked to solve a case abstain when the input is defective, and when it does not, can the same model catch the defect when asked instead to verify the input? We study six recent models on SARA-derived tax cases under missing-fact and contradictory-fact perturbations. The strongest models abstain when a fact is missing but compute through injected contradiction

translated_title: 求解与验证之辨：捕捉税务推理系统中的矛盾
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型如今在法定基准测试中，能够对超过90%的格式良好案例计算出正确的应纳税额，这使它们成为直接消费此类答案的税务咨询与合规系统的候选方案。然而，真实的法律输入往往存在缺陷：所需事实缺失，或已陈述的事实相互矛盾。模型在干净基准上的准确率无法说明其在面对此类输入时的表现，而一个对有缺陷输入直接进行计算的系统，会返回一个看似可信的数字，却没有任何出错的迹象。由此引出两个问题：当输入存在缺陷时，被要求求解案例的模型是否会弃答；当模型不弃答时，若改为要求同一模型验证输入，它能否捕捉到缺陷？我们在事实缺失和事实矛盾两种扰动条件下，研究了六个近期模型在源自SARA的税务案例上的表现。最强的模型在事实缺失时能够弃答，但会对注入的矛盾直接进行计算
tldr: 该研究揭示大型语言模型在税务推理中虽能在事实缺失时正确弃答，却无法察觉事实之间的矛盾，说明“验证”任务并不能弥补“求解”任务中忽视矛盾的缺陷。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that large language models in tax reasoning can abstain when facts are missing but fail to catch contradictory facts, showing that verification does not compensate for the blind spot of solving through contradictions.
